Requirement Statement: The firmware shall ignore unrecognized or malformed UART commands without changing the system state.
Source Text / Evidence:
UART: 115200 baud, 8-N-1. Required commands:
MOTOR START
MOTOR STOP
SPEED <RPM>
DIR CW / DIR CCW
STATUS
Report state, target/estimated speed, direction and fault status
Inference Rationale: Only the listed commands are defined. Without explicit handling for invalid or malformed input, the controller could enter unintended states or accept partial inputs, undermining safe and verifiable command/control via UART.
Acceptance Criteria: Send malformed/unknown strings (e.g., "STAR", "SPEED 42a", truncated frames) while observing STATUS; verify state, target speed, direction and fault status remain unchanged before and after the inputs.
Preconditions: UART link established; system in a known state (STOPPED or RUN).
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: System state and parameters unchanged after invalid inputs.
Comments / Open Questions: Whether an explicit error response should be returned for invalid commands is not specified.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall reject SPEED commands outside 300–1000 RPM and shall not change the target speed in response.
Source Text / Evidence:
- Support configurable speed command from 300 to 1000 RPM.
SPEED <RPM>
Set target speed
Inference Rationale: The PRD defines an allowed range but not the behavior for out-of-range inputs. Rejecting them is necessary to avoid undefined operation and to make verification of the range requirement objective.
Acceptance Criteria: With target speed set to a valid value, send SPEED 200 and SPEED 1100; verify STATUS shows target speed unchanged and no transition in system state.
Preconditions: System initialized; any valid target speed previously set.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Target speed unchanged after out-of-range SPEED commands.
Comments / Open Questions: Whether to emit an error/acknowledgment for rejected SPEED values is unspecified.

Requirement Statement: If a direction change is commanded while the motor is running, the firmware shall perform a controlled deceleration to zero speed before applying torque in the new direction.
Source Text / Evidence:
- CW and CCW operation
- Controlled motor stop
Inference Rationale: The PRD requires controlled stops and operation in both directions but is silent on mid-run reversals. Without an explicit reversal policy, a DIR change at speed can cause abrupt reverse torque, violating the "controlled" stop criterion and risking hardware stress.
Acceptance Criteria: With motor running CW at a steady in-range speed, send DIR CCW; verify speed decelerates to 0 RPM before any reverse torque is applied, then accelerates CCW. No reverse-torque spikes prior to zero crossing.
Preconditions: Motor running within specified speed range.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Direction reversed only after passing through zero speed.
Failure Behavior: If reversal sequencing cannot be achieved, the controller shall refuse the direction change and maintain current direction.
Comments / Open Questions: No deceleration rate or maximum reversal time specified.

Category: Drive Safety, Fault Handling & Reset Protection
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall prevent motor start and shall stop the motor and disable PWM when the measured DC supply voltage is outside the configured allowable range.
Source Text / Evidence: - No operation outside configured voltage/current limits
Inference Rationale: SF-003 prohibits operation outside configured limits but does not specify the concrete inhibit/stop actions for voltage violations. This decomposition is required to make the limit enforceable and testable.
Acceptance Criteria: With configured voltage limits, vary the DC supply below the minimum and above the maximum: (a) START is refused when out of range; (b) if running, the drive is disabled and STATUS indicates a fault upon crossing the threshold.
Preconditions: Voltage limit thresholds configured; means of measuring supply voltage available.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Drive disabled or start inhibited while voltage remains out of range.
Failure Behavior: Remain disabled until voltage returns within range and a new START command is issued.
Comments / Open Questions: Exact voltage thresholds and measurement source/channel are not specified in the PRD.

Category: Drive Safety, Fault Handling & Reset Protection
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall detect loss or out-of-range behavior of phase current measurements (e.g., disconnection, saturation, rail) and immediately disable PWM, entering a fault state.
Source Text / Evidence:
- Measure motor phase current using the IHM16M1 current-sensing circuitry.
- Detect motor-control faults and immediately disable PWM output.
Inference Rationale: FOC relies on accurate phase currents; if current sensing fails, continued drive can cause uncontrolled torque and overcurrent. Explicit detection and shutdown are required to meet the PRD’s fault shutdown intent.
Acceptance Criteria: Induce sensor faults (disconnect shunt signal, force ADC reading to rail, disable ADC DMA) while running; verify PWM is disabled with no further drive pulses and STATUS indicates a faulted state.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: System enters FAULT state with drive disabled.
Failure Behavior: Remain disabled until fault is cleared and START is reissued.
Comments / Open Questions: Maximum allowable detection/shutdown latency is not specified.

Category: Drive Safety, Fault Handling & Reset Protection
Requirement Statement: On any MCU reset, watchdog reset, or brown-out event, the firmware shall ensure PWM outputs are disabled and the motor remains stopped until initialization completes and a valid START command is received.
Source Text / Evidence:
- Motor shall remain stopped after system initialization.
- Detect motor-control faults and immediately disable PWM output.
- Immediate PWM shutdown on motor-driver fault
Inference Rationale: The PRD requires the motor be stopped after initialization and PWM be disabled on faults. Resets and brown-outs can occur asynchronously; without an explicit safe-state requirement, spurious drive pulses could occur during or after reset.
Acceptance Criteria: Induce a watchdog reset and a brown-out while running; verify no PWM activity during reset and after reboot until a new START command is issued; STATUS reports STOPPED before any START.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: PWM outputs inactive; motor remains stopped until commanded to start.
Comments / Open Questions: Definition of brown-out detection source/threshold on the chosen hardware is not specified.

Category: Drive Safety, Fault Handling & Reset Protection
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall enable a watchdog that resets the MCU if the control software fails to service it within a configured interval, ensuring fail-safe shutdown of the drive on software hang.
Source Text / Evidence:
- Detect motor-control faults and immediately disable PWM output.
- Immediate PWM shutdown on motor-driver fault
Inference Rationale: A hung firmware cannot execute fault handling to disable PWM. A watchdog is necessary to restore the system to a known safe state consistent with the PRD’s shutdown intent.
Acceptance Criteria: Introduce a deliberate software hang while running; verify the watchdog resets the MCU and, after reboot, the motor remains stopped until a new START command is received.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: System resets; PWM disabled after reset until commanded to start.
Comments / Open Questions: Watchdog timeout value and selection of independent vs. windowed watchdog are not specified.

Requirement Statement: When a fault is present, the STATUS response shall include a fault code that identifies the fault category (e.g., undervoltage limit, overcurrent limit, sensor fault, startup failure).
Source Text / Evidence:
STATUS
Report state, target/estimated speed, direction and fault status
Inference Rationale: The PRD requires reporting "fault status" but without a code the user and testers cannot determine which limit or fault occurred, making verification of limit enforcement and fault handling impractical.
Acceptance Criteria: Induce representative faults (voltage limit violation, current limit saturation, current-sense fault, startup timeout) and verify STATUS includes a non-null code that matches the induced category.
Preconditions: STATUS command available; fault-inducing test setup prepared.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: STATUS reports a category code corresponding to the active fault.
Comments / Open Questions: Fault code enumeration and mapping are not defined in the PRD.

Requirement Statement: If the motor fails to achieve sustained rotation within a bounded startup time or number of attempts from standstill, the firmware shall declare a startup fault and disable PWM.
Source Text / Evidence: - Reliable motor startup from standstill
Inference Rationale: To make "reliable startup" verifiable and safe, the controller must detect startup failure and stop driving rather than retry indefinitely, which could overheat the motor or driver and mask faults.
Acceptance Criteria: With conditions that prevent startup (e.g., rotor locked, extreme load, incorrect parameters), issue MOTOR START; verify the controller aborts within a bounded interval/attempt count, disables PWM, and STATUS indicates a startup fault.
Parameters / Constraints: Maximum startup time or attempt count
Preconditions: System at standstill; within configured operating limits except the induced startup-preventing condition.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Drive disabled; fault latched until cleared and a new START is issued.
Comments / Open Questions: Startup timeout/attempt thresholds are not specified in the PRD.
